name: JPEG dimples
corpus: synthetic photo-like scenes generated from fixed seeds (forensic.validation.run.scene)

detection.task: Does the JPEG carry a camera encoder's dimple? Where is it missing?
detection.positives: 40 images through an emulated dimple-making encoder (constant DCT bias before quantisation, quality 75/85/95), at three bias strengths
detection.negatives: the same 40 images saved once by libjpeg, and decoded and saved twice by libjpeg

localisation.cases: 40 emulated camera originals (bias 0.5) with 30% x 30% pasted from a libjpeg-saved photo, re-saved at 90 or 95
localisation.detected_means: the local warning is raised and at least 30% of the pasted area is marked as lacking the dimple

real_camera_originals.note: No ground truth: shows how common dimples are among these cameras and that re-saving does not reliably remove them.
real_camera_originals.source: the first JPEG of each camera folder in the digicam corpus (drewnoakes/digicam_corpus, CC0, commit 6385e5e)

known_failure_modes: Many cameras make no dimple; absence alone shows nothing.
On real cameras the dimple often survives re-saving by software, so presence does not show the file is the camera original (see real_camera_originals).
Synthetic positives come from an emulated encoder; real dimple strengths vary by camera model.
Flat, saturated and very dark areas carry no dimple and are hatched in the map.
